You hear an A&E doctor briefing a colleague about a patient.
 The A&E doctor
A. thinks that the cough medication is causing the patient’s rash
B. thinks that the absence of other symptoms is unusual
C. thinks that further investigation is necessary

You hear a dermatologist in a training session with an intern.
 Why does the dermatologist ask about the next step?
A. Because the patient is in pain due to his condition
B. Because he wants to hear the intern’s recommendation
C. Because he wants to hear the intern’s diagnosis

You hear an intern asking a senior doctor about the diagnosis of a patient.
 How does the senior doctor deal with the intern’s concern?
A. By telling her that she is looking at the wrong symptoms
B. By helping her to reexamine the patient’s symptoms
C. By telling her to be sure of what the symptoms of Parkinson’s are

You hear a morning briefing in a ward.
 What does the doctor prioritise for the patient’s care?
A. Helping the patient with his balance problems
B. Getting a neurologist to confirm a diagnosis
C. Learning more about the patient’s background

You hear two radiologists discussing the possible diagnosis of a patient.
 What does the female doctor describe?
A. A plain radiograph showing the patient’s skull
B. A CT scan showing an abnormality
C. A patient with a rare disease

You hear a patient expressing a concern to an occupational therapist.
 What does the patient wish to be able to do?
A. Walk up the stairs without using a hand rail
B. Support herself using her right arm
C. Be able to take a shower by herself

Why does the speaker mention the rate of incidence of IBS?
A. She wants to show the audience that it is an important condition.
B. She wants to show that Australians are more likely to have the
 condition.
C. She wants to show that women are more likely to develop the
 condition.

Why are potential IBS sufferers tested for other diseases?
A. Because there are other diseases more common than IBS.
B. Because there is no direct way to test for IBS.
C. Because there are diseases that generally co-present with IBS.

Why does the speaker say IBS is a difficult disease to manage?
A. It is not possible to know which symptoms will occur or when.
B. It is not possible to diagnose patients with the condition.
C. It is not possible to lessen the negative impact it has on patients.

What warning does the speaker give about a low-FODMAP diet?
A. It can be dangerous for some patients with gastrointestinal
 problems.
B. It includes foods that most people do not enjoy eating.
C. It may not be effective for all patients suffering from IBS.

Why is it difficult to stick to a low-FODMAP diet?
A. There are many popular foods which are high-FODMAPs.
B. There are no low-FODMAP products available.
C. There are few places to buy low-FODMAP foods.

According to the speaker, what effect can high-FODMAP foods have on
 the digestive system?
A. They cause the gut to attract water, release gas and stretch the
 intestines.
B. They cause the gut to process the food slower than usual and
 breed bacteria.
C. They cause the gut to expand due to high levels of water and gas.

According to the speaker, the most important challenge facing
 dermatology is…
A. The financial aspect of seeking treatment
B. The low priority placed on the specialty
C. The lack of contributions made by the specialty

Why does the speaker mention skin cancer and women’s health?
A. To give examples of priorities in dermatology
B. To give examples of failures in dermatology
C. To give examples of the importance of dermatology

According to the speaker, what is needed to increase the number of
 dermatology residents?
A. A way to increase the number of residency positions available
B. A way to fund more residency positions in the specialty
C. A way to train new dermatologists more efficiently than currently

According to the speaker, how is dermatology perceived by
 policymakers?
A. There is a perception that the specialty is only for the rich and
 famous.
B. There is an old-fashioned perception of the specialty.
C. There is a perception that the specialty lacks diversity.

Other physicians have responded to the shortage of dermatologists...
A. By treating dermatological disorders themselves
B. By not referring their patients to dermatologists
C. By recognizing the need for more dermatologists

According to the speaker, who or what is overly involved in
 dermatological research?
A. Pharmaceutical industry
B. Research funders
C. Doctors of other specialities
